A1.justification: Both PDFs describe XModBench. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, modality analyses, failure cases, dual-context experiments, and a human study in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds baseline evaluations, XModBench-Lite results, and evaluation-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The aligned triplets, six context–candidate modality configurations, and three-stage construction pipeline remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies that GPT-5 edits question wording without changing semantics; it does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same five task families, 17 subtasks, data sources, and language coverage. XModBench-Lite uses retained coverage; revised sample counts and the no-context control concern evaluation settings.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 2 and 4 add Qwen2.5-VL, Intern3.5-VL, and a no-context baseline. The two vision–language models are evaluated only in the text–vision directions. The original full-benchmark model and human comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix A introduces a balanced 6,000-question evaluation with 200 examples per task-family/modality-direction combination, and v2 adds a no-context control. The reported full-benchmark size changes from 60,828 to 61,320 questions, with revised subtask counts in Figure 2. These reported changes do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new no-context results add a context-removal control, reporting approximately chance-level accuracy. The original modality-disparity, directional-imbalance, failure-case, and dual-context analyses remain; displaying dual-context results in the main text does not constitute a new experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across modality configurations as diagnostic spread and disclose 10 valid human participants per subtask/configuration. Neither adds repeated-run uncertainty, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds a complete Lite results table, full-benchmark results for the new comparators, and token/runtime measurements. The original numerical results are preserved: v1 Table 2 matches v2 Table 5, and the detailed subtask and dual-context tables also match. Lite scores are new results under different sampling conditions, not same-setting performance changes; several new averages are internally inconsistent.

T1.justification: The modality-disparity and directional-imbalance definitions and formulas remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central benchmark contribution and headline findings about audio weakness, reasoning limitations, and directional asymmetry. The revised question count does not change the contribution's substantive scope.

C2.justification: New Section 5 attributes performance patterns to interleaved training, speech-focused data, missing task coverage, and post-training erosion of alignment. It develops substantial model-development interpretations absent from v1, while acknowledging opaque training data. These explanations use existing comparisons rather than new controlled training experiments.

D1.justification: New Appendix D reports token usage, runtime, and an eight-A6000 setup with one process per GPU. v2 adds explicit dataset and code links, clarifies GPT-5's editing role, and states that releases exclude copyrighted audiovisual material. The original detailed data-processing appendix is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Radford et al. on speech recognition and Shao et al. on reinforcement learning, supporting the new training-related discussion. The related-work section and central novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Changes include localized wording and terminology edits, a new interpretive section and ethics statement, an appendix contents page, and updated publication and corresponding-author information.

P2.justification: The dense main results table moves to Appendix B and is replaced by a compact summary organized by task family and modality direction. v2 also adds Lite and cost tables, redisplays dual-context results in the main text, moves Figure 1 before the abstract, and updates Figure 2. These substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves navigation and adds useful controls, resource information, and a smaller evaluation option while preserving the original results. However, its new Lite table contains substantial inconsistencies: Qwen2.5-Omni's task and modality scores both average about 59.8%, but Table 4 reports 51.4% despite the stated balanced design. The new training explanations also lack controlled supporting experiments. These benefits and reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
